subject: Appeal: temporary allocation for Castor Health sprint backfill
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna@castorhealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@castorhealth.com
Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary capacity for Oct 28-31 sprint backfill

Hi Rishi,

Quick note from Castor — we had an unexpected compliance patch that stalled three teams. They need additional inference headroom for Oct 28-31 to re-run validation and end-to-end QA. Our forecast (attached) shows ~18M additional tokens across the window, peak concurrency expected 20 rps for 6 hours/day.

We know this is short notice but are requesting either:
- a temporary reserved carveout for the 28-31 window, or
- an exemption to the autoscale burst cap to avoid throttling.

Procurement is ready to sign a short SOW amendment for a 3-day addendum with prorated fees if that helps. Attached: castor_forecast_oct_weeks.csv and a draft SOW request.

Can you advise next steps and whether ops/product need to approve?

Thanks,
Anna Lopez
Head of Platform Engineering
Castor Health

Thanks Anna — looping in Product (Kimberly) and Capacity (Laura + Dev) to evaluate options. A few quick clarifying Qs so we can scope the ask and surface the least disruptive path: 

1) Is the 20 rps peak sustained across all models or concentrated on one model family?
2) Do you require guaranteed latency SLOs (p50/p95) or is throughput the main priority?
3) If we offer a temporary reserved slice, will Castor sign the 3-day SOW amendment by EOD 27th?

We can move fast on a short carveout if procurement signs. If not, we can explore a temporary burst-cap increase but need to confirm impact to other reserved pools.

Rishi

Thanks for flagging — quick assessment from Product/Capacity policy perspective:

Summary:
- Peak is manageable if it's concentrated on a single model family and Castor can accept p95 around 400-500ms during the 6-hour peak windows.
- A 3-day reserved slice (~8 GPUs equivalent) would cost ~prorated 0.16 of their monthly Dedicated commit.

Options (ranked):
1) Short reserved carveout (preferred) — clean isolation, minimal risk to other customers, needs SOW signed and ops playbook updated.
2) Temporary burst cap increase — faster to approve but higher risk for noisy neighbor impact and will require routing policy adjustments.
3) KV-prefix caching + request router tweaks — lower cost but only helps if workloads reuse prefixes.

Action items for Rishi:
- Get confirmation on model distribution and whether latency SLOs are required.
- If Castor signs, Ops needs a ticket by 27th EOD to pre-stage the slice.

I can draft the SOW amendment language with legal if needed — happy to own that with Laura.

-Kim
Director, Product
Redwood Inference

Hi team — Ops perspective and practical plan: 

We can provision a temporary slice using the short-reserve flow; estimated work: 2 hours pre-stage, cutover script run 30 minutes before window, teardown script post-window. Risks:
- If burst increase chosen instead, we must throttle other pilot lanes via routing precedence which requires owner approval (impact emails to 3 pilots).

Proposed timeline: 
- Wed 28 Oct 08:00 PT: pre-stage (reserve resources, warm caches).
- Wed 28 Oct 11:30 PT: cutover and validation with Castor test traffic.
- Thu 29 Oct 06:00 PT: standby, monitor.
- Fri 31 Oct 18:00 PT: teardown.

Laura will own runbook + postmortem. Ops needs: signed SOW + final model list + any IP/data residency constraints (Castor).

Attachments: ops_runbook_template.md (stub referenced in drive link).

Laura Bennett
Capacity Operations Manager
